lines: XC01: Connect Sites to the DAM with OpenAPI [one-time]
AS01: DAM onboarding, users and access [one-time]
AS05: Content Hub portal for approved assets [one-time]
sections: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI lets Sites authors use approved assets from a remote AEM Assets environment in the Page Editor (remote assets in Content Fragments work on AEM 6.5, not on AEM as a Cloud Service); Adobe recommends it over the older Connected Assets.

Authors place brand-approved images from the DAM onto pages built with the Image v3 and Teaser v2 components (other components need custom work), and changes to approved assets reach the live site without re-uploading.
We will set the asset delivery repository and IMS client variables in Cloud Manager, configure the Image v3 component and HTTPS, and confirm authors can pick remote assets.
We will add users to the Admin Console, create user groups and attach the AEM Assets product profiles, and confirm the Cloud Manager program and environments for the DAM.
We will deploy Content Hub, set user, contributor and administrator roles, configure the portal, and set up the approval step that releases assets to it.

We will work through Adobe's go-live checklist: a production pipeline with functional and UI tests, Dispatcher validation, CDN, SSL and DNS, performance and security tests on stage, notification profiles and traffic filter rules.

lines: XC10: Connect AEM Sites to Commerce with CIF [one-time]
AS01: DAM onboarding, users and access [one-time]
SI01: Cloud Manager program, pipelines and access [one-time]
sections: The Commerce Integration Framework (CIF) add-on, provisioned by Adobe, connects AEM Sites as a Cloud Service to the Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoint so authors can search, browse and use product data in AEM. It suits headless AEM content and existing CIF sites: the CIF storefront and CIF Core Components are in maintenance mode, and Adobe recommends Edge Delivery with the Commerce Storefront for new storefronts, while documenting a headless AEM storefront that starts with the CIF add-on.
Authors find real products from the Commerce catalog while building headless content, and pages on existing CIF sites, so shopping content uses live product data instead of copied details.
We will once Adobe provisions the CIF add-on, set the COMMERCE_ENDPOINT variable for each environment in Cloud Manager and the CIF configuration for store view and catalog root.

We will build the commerce-specific content (product teasers, category and campaign content, Content Fragments) that authors assemble from products they search and browse in AEM, using Content Fragments and headless content for new builds rather than CIF Core Components.
We will add users to the Admin Console, create user groups and attach the AEM Assets product profiles, and confirm the Cloud Manager program and environments for the DAM.
We will assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager, set up Git access and the first deployment pipelines.

Our approach
- The Commerce Integration Framework (CIF) add-on, provisioned by Adobe, connects AEM Sites as a Cloud Service to the Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoint so authors can search, browse and use product data in AEM. It suits headless AEM content and existing CIF sites: the CIF storefront and CIF Core Components are in maintenance mode, and Adobe recommends Edge Delivery with the Commerce Storefront for new storefronts, while documenting a headless AEM storefront that starts with the CIF add-on.
- Authors find real products from the Commerce catalog while building headless content, and pages on existing CIF sites, so shopping content uses live product data instead of copied details.

What we would do
- We will once Adobe provisions the CIF add-on, set the COMMERCE_ENDPOINT variable for each environment in Cloud Manager and the CIF configuration for store view and catalog root.
- We will build the commerce-specific content (product teasers, category and campaign content, Content Fragments) that authors assemble from products they search and browse in AEM, using Content Fragments and headless content for new builds rather than CIF Core Components.
- We will add users to the Admin Console, create user groups and attach the AEM Assets product profiles, and confirm the Cloud Manager program and environments for the DAM.
- We will assign AEM product profiles in the Admin Console, create the production program and environments in Cloud Manager, set up Git access and the first deployment pipelines.

candidates.label: Approved AEM Assets images sync to Commerce products by SKU (Adobe's extension on Commerce on Cloud and on-premises; built into Commerce as a Cloud Service)
candidates.how: The AEM Assets Integration for Commerce links approved AEM Assets to Commerce products by SKU, or by custom matching built in Adobe Developer App Builder, and syncs them into the catalog; merchandisers can also pick DAM assets inside the Commerce Admin. On Commerce on Cloud and on-premises it's an Adobe extension the partner installs; on Commerce as a Cloud Service it's configured in the Commerce Admin.
candidates.gain: Merchandisers manage product images once in AEM Assets; approved images tagged with SKUs reach Commerce products, most within five minutes, keeping storefronts accurate and on brand.
